source_excerpt:
Gives rural youth opportunities to take part in village development and local governance.
Builds leadership, teamwork and organisational skills through training and youth activities.
Runs cultural, sports, health, environmental and skill-development programmes at the village and block level.
Spreads awareness against addiction, superstition and other social issues while encouraging community service.
Rural youth can contact their Gram Panchayat or the Yuva Protsahan Kendra at their Janpad Panchayat office.
The Chhattisgarh Swami Vivekanand Yuva Protsahan Yojana is a youth development scheme launched by the Government of Chhattisgarh on 20 June 2013. The Panchayat and Rural Development Department introduced the scheme to promote positive thinking, creativity and leadership among rural youth. It also encourages young people to participate in village development and local governance.
The scheme supports various youth development activities. These include cultural programmes, sports, yoga, educational awareness and health campaigns. It also promotes sanitation, environmental protection and community service. Young people can participate in awareness campaigns against addiction, superstition and other social problems.
The Chhattisgarh Swami Vivekanand Yuva Protsahan Yojana aims to develop leadership, teamwork and organisational skills. It also promotes moral values and social responsibility. Youth groups and clubs at the Gram Panchayat level encourage young people to participate in community development. Janpad Panchayats help plan and coordinate these activities.
Each Janpad Panchayat operates a Yuva Protsahan Kendra (Youth Promotion Centre) to support youth development and training. The scheme's reported funding structure provides an annual grant of around ₹6 lakh per Janpad Panchayat. Youth associated with registered Gram Panchayat-level Yuva Mandals can participate in scheme activities. Other interested youth can contact their local Yuva Protsahan Kendra to enquire about registration and participation.
The scheme focuses on youth training, leadership and community development rather than direct monthly cash assistance. Young people can contact their Gram Panchayat or the concerned Janpad Panchayat to learn about registration, required documents and available programmes. Those seeking financial support for self-employment can also explore the Chhattisgarh Udhyam Kranti Yojana , a separate initiative.
The Chhattisgarh Swami Vivekanand Yuva Protsahan Yojana promotes youth development, leadership and community participation through various activities organised at the local level. Its key benefits include:
Encourages young people to participate in village development and local governance.
Promotes personality development, leadership skills and teamwork among rural youth.
Supports cultural programmes, sports, yoga, education, health, environmental protection and sanitation activities.
Creates awareness about social issues, including addiction, superstition and other social evils.
Encourages young people to participate in community service, disaster response and training programmes on modern agricultural practices.
Types of Activities Organised Under the Scheme
The Chhattisgarh Swami Vivekanand Yuva Protsahan Yojana promotes youth development through cultural events, leadership training, sports and community service. The major activities under the scheme include the following:
Organising youth cultural festivals at block and sub-block levels.
Holding folk music, singing, dance and drama or skit competitions.
Conducting singing, dance and drama training camps for rural youth.
Conducting creative leadership training camps for Yuva Mandal representatives.
Organising life-skills education workshops for adolescent girls.
Holding workshops on planning and managing voluntary community development activities.
Organising tree-plantation and blood-donation camps.
Encouraging youth to participate in sanitation and literacy campaigns.
Mobilising volunteers for vaccination drives and health-awareness programmes.
Conducting yoga-training camps for young people.
Organising volleyball, kabaddi and kho-kho competitions.
Holding athletics competitions, including races, high jump, long jump and swimming.
Arranging practice camps for selected young athletes.
Organising workshops on organic farming and modern agricultural techniques.
Mobilising youth volunteers during disasters such as floods, fires and epidemics.
Conducting awareness rallies against addiction, social evils and superstition.
In practice, this has funded things like employment fairs, open-gym equipment at government schools, bamboo-craft and mushroom-production training, Kabaddi tournaments with cash prizes, and army-recruitment pre-training camps.
Applicants interested in participating in the Chhattisgarh Swami Vivekanand Yuva Protsahan Yojana should meet the following tentative eligibility requirements:
The applicant should be a young person residing in a rural area of Chhattisgarh.
The applicant should be between 15 and 35 years of age.
The applicant should be associated with a youth group or youth club formed or registered at the Gram Panchayat level, as applicable.
Youth who are not yet part of a Yuva Mandal can also register directly
The scheme applies only to rural areas of the state; it does not cover urban youth
The applicant should be willing to participate in youth development activities, training programmes, cultural events, sports and community service activities organised under the scheme.
Unlike most government schemes, the Swami Vivekanand Yuva Protsahan Yojana does not ask for a bundle of supporting certificates. It only asks for the details below, filled into the scheme's own registration form.
A recent passport-size photograph, to be affixed to the registration form
Basic personal details: full name, father's name, date of birth, complete address and a contact number
Caste category (SC/ST/OBC/General), as recorded on the registration form
The field or skill area in which the applicant wants training
Details of any prior achievements or notable work, if applicable
Name of the Yuva Mandal, if the applicant is already a member of one
Official guidelines do not ask for any additional certificate, such as an income or residence proof, beyond the details captured on this one registration form
Young people interested in participating in the Chhattisgarh Swami Vivekanand Yuva Protsahan Yojana can contact their local Gram Panchayat or the concerned Janpad Panchayat to enquire about youth group registration and participation in scheme activities. The following steps provide a tentative guide based on the scheme's Panchayat-level implementation arrangements.
Check whether your Gram Panchayat already has a registered Yuva Mandal (youth association). If you're already a member, you're automatically included in the scheme.
If you're not yet part of a Yuva Mandal, visit the Yuva Protsahan Kendra at your Janpad Panchayat office.
Collect the official Swami Vivekanand Yuva Protsahan Yojana registration form from the Yuva Protsahan Kendra or the Janpad Panchayat CEO's office.
Fill in your personal details, educational qualification, and your preferred area of skill-development training.
Attach a passport-size photograph to the form.
Submit the completed form to the Convenor or Co-Convenor of the Yuva Protsahan Kendra.
Once registered, you'll be given a registration number and can take part in the training programmes and activities the Janpad Panchayat organises throughout the year.
Important: These steps are a general guide based on the scheme's reported registration arrangements. Confirm the current application procedure, registration requirements and responsible office with the concerned Panchayat before applying.

1. What is the Chhattisgarh Swami Vivekanand Yuva Protsahan Yojana?
The Chhattisgarh Swami Vivekanand Yuva Protsahan Yojana is a youth development scheme, which promotes leadership, creativity, sports and community participation among rural youth.
2. Who can benefit from the Chhattisgarh Swami Vivekanand Yuva Protsahan Yojana?
Rural youth in Chhattisgarh can participate in youth development activities through local youth groups and clubs. Interested applicants should confirm the current eligibility rules with their Gram Panchayat or Janpad Panchayat.
3. What are the benefits of the Swami Vivekanand Yuva Protsahan Yojana?
The scheme supports cultural programmes, sports, yoga, health awareness, environmental protection, sanitation and community service. It also helps develop leadership and teamwork skills.
4. Does the Chhattisgarh Swami Vivekanand Yuva Protsahan Yojana provide financial assistance to individuals?
The scheme focuses on youth development, training and community activities. The available scheme report does not establish a fixed monthly cash benefit for individual youth.
A Yuva Protsahan Kendra, or Youth Promotion Centre, supports youth development and training activities at the Janpad Panchayat level.
6. How can I apply for the Chhattisgarh Swami Vivekanand Yuva Protsahan Yojana?
Contact your local Gram Panchayat or the concerned Janpad Panchayat to ask about youth group registration, the application form and available activities.
7. Can I apply for Swami Vivekanand Yuva Protsahan Yojana online?
No. This scheme has no online application portal. Registration happens offline, through your Gram Panchayat's Yuva Mandal or the Yuva Protsahan Kendra at your Janpad Panchayat.
8. I'm already part of a youth club in my village. Do I need to register again?
If your village's youth club is a Yuva Mandal registered at the Gram Panchayat level, you're already included under this scheme and don't need a fresh registration.
9. Is there an income limit to join this scheme?
No. The official guideline does not set any income limit for rural youth to be part of this scheme.
10. Can non-student rural youth also be part of this scheme?
Yes. Eligibility is based only on age (15 to 35 years) and rural residence in Chhattisgarh, it isn't restricted to students.
